This wiki has a new extension: [https://github.com/lethosor/DFDiagram DFDiagram]!

This is an expanded (and possibly more efficient) replacement for {{tl|diagram}}. Features include:
* An unlimited number of diagrams per page ({{tl|diagram}} depends on RegexFunctions, so it is limited by the Regex functions limit)
* Basic tileset support (transparency and creature graphics don't work, but all of the non-transparent tilesets in the [[tileset repository]] should work)
* Z-levels
* A variety of new syntax features:
** Variables
** Special characters
** DF-style colors (e.g. 7:0 for light grey)

There are a couple differences between this and {{tl|diagram}}:
* Colors persist until explicitly changed (use [#] to reset the foreground color):
{| class="wikitable"
|-
! Code !! {{tl|diagram}} !! &lt;diagram>
|-
| [#f00]red text
| {{diagram|[#f00]red text}}
| <diagram>[#f00]red text</diagram>
|}

See the [https://github.com/lethosor/DFDiagram/wiki wiki] for more in-depth help.

An example:
<diagram>
<frame type="level" level="0">
[#2:0][@ffffd0]This is a sample diagram[#@]
This diagram has multiple z-levels! Press
< to go up one z-level.
</frame>
<frame type=level level=1>
[$cat=c]
This is z-level 1.
Here is a dwarf: [%01]
Here are a lot of dwarves: [%01][%01][%01][%01][%02][%01][%01][%01][%02][%01][%01][%02][%02][%01][%01]
Here is a cat: [#0:1][$cat][#]
Here is a green cat: [#2:1][$cat][#]
Press < to go up one more z-level.
</frame>
<frame type=level level=2>
This is z-level 2.
Notice how the diagram size changes depending on the content of each z-level.
</frame>
</diagram>
